newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan leader due to meet Dostum, Taleban chief.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan leader due to meet Dostum, Taleban chief.

text.p: Pakistani President Farooq Leghari was due to meet Afghan Taleban militia leader Mullah Mohammad Omar and Uzbek chief General Abdul Rashid Dostum in Uzbekistan's capital Tashkent on Saturday in a fresh attempt to halt fighting in Afghanistan, Pakistani newspapers said.

They said Leghari, who arrived in Tashkent on Friday, had already held talks with Uzbek President Islam Karimov in which the two men agreed that formation of a broad-based government representing all Afghan ethnic and religious groups was the best way to achieve peace in Afghanistan.
Pakistani Interior Minister Naseerullah Babar arranged the first public talks between Taleban leaders and Dostum in the northern Afghan city of Mazar-i-Sharif on Wednesday.
Further talks took place on Thursday in the southern Afghan city of Kandahar, where the reclusive Omar has his headquarters.
Pakistan has focused its diplomatic efforts on preventing fighting between the radical Islamic Taleban and Dostum's forces since the Taleban captured Kabul on September 27.

Last week, Dostum signed a defence pact with ousted government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood and Shi'ite Moslem leader Karim Khalili. On Friday, his troops helped those of Masood recapture Bagram airbase north of Kabul, according to a spokesman for Masood.
